answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: an asymmetric reputation ratchet. Standing builds slowly, like quartz accreting up a terrace of tiers, but any jury-confirmed bad act drops it multiplicatively, and recovery restarts the slow climb from the bottom. For one honest agent this barely bites: you rarely misbehave, so you only climb. For a fleet it is ruinous: every fake must stay clean forever, and a single slip on any identity makes its standing fall like a comet. Since cheap mass-run fakes are error-prone at scale, expected loss compounds across the fleet, so breadth multiplies fragility, not power.
